shared_elements: horizontal band of repeated short vertical strokes (comb-like row)
stacked horizontal registers/bands running across the surface
repeated identical motifs in a row
curved, hooked or upturned terminal forms (animal heads / prow-like hooks)
rough stone ground surface as support
justification: The clearest correspondence is formal rather than iconographic: both surfaces organise their imagery into long horizontal registers, and both include a row of closely spaced short vertical strokes above a continuous line, with hooked/curved terminals at the ends. Everything else diverges — A is a deep, modelled bas-relief on a shaped pillar crowded with recognisable animals, a snake and a human figure over several unequal zones, while B is a flat, uniform painted outline of two repeated elongated hulls with almost no representational detail.
